name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz impeded; Iran orders tighter closure
summary: Iran's army ordered Hormuz closed 'further day by day' on 23 Nov; IRGC claims three tankers hit mines under US escort
state: Iran's army chief Amir Hatami ordered the navy on 23 Nov to close the Strait of Hormuz further day by day until Iran's conditions are met, and the IRGC said three tankers under US air escort hit mines, which the JMIC called unconfirmed (Euronews, 24 Nov). JMIC recorded 114 US-assisted passages on 19–21 Nov. UKMTO said on 10 Nov that traffic was about 65% below pre-conflict levels (Gulf News), and at least 10 ships were hit in the first ten days of November (Reuters via Canberra Times). Hormuz traffic stays materially impeded.
for_you: Shipping and energy markets face continued disruption through the Gulf. Seafarers and travellers in the region can check FCDO travel advice and UKMTO guidance.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (UKMTO ~65% below pre-conflict; closure order 23 Nov)

sources.title: Euronews — Iran orders Hormuz closed 'further day by day' as Qatar seeks to revive peace talks
Gulf News — Hormuz shipping 'below normal, but not stalled': UKMTO
The Canberra Times (Reuters/AAP) — Iran's military reports explosions on two oil tankers

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
